notes: Panel 1 is the frame painted before any command: nothing here proves the new keys were applied at startup, which is exactly why panel 2 exists.

Panel 2 opens `/settings`. Its rows are built from the *live* App (`app.thinking_visible()`, `app.autocomplete_max_visible()`), so the text is the visible proof that startup applied the file rather than the built-in defaults.
The `probe` rows name post-fix behaviour; on a pre-fix binary they report XFAIL instead of failing the run, which is how one scenario documents both sides of the A/B.
The quiet-startup row is asserted separately by lum1310-quiet-startup-{on,off}.json, because it is read before the App exists and therefore cannot be proven from inside the modal.
caption: LUM-1310 — hideThinkingBlock + autocompleteMaxVisible applied from settings.json at startup. Prepared HOME says `hideThinkingBlock: true, autocompleteMaxVisible: 10`; `/settings` reads the live App, so `Hide thinking  true` / `Autocomplete max items  10` can only appear if the file was read before the first frame. Pre-fix the same scenario reports `false` / `5`. Real binary + real PTY + pyte VT emulator; nothing mocked.

panels.label: 1. idle 120x34 — the frame painted before any command runs
2. /settings — the new rows read the running App: thinking + dropdown height come from the file
